guide.title: Structure and design decisions
guide.summary: The v0.1 source contract, link model, and deliberately limited scope.

section.title: Purpose
section.p: ASM defines a corpus that independently built tools can consume without an LLM, a hosted service, or this repository's Python code. The builder is a reference implementation of the documented format. This is a design goal; no empirical validity or established ecosystem is claimed.

section.title: Source layout
section.p: All manual content is canonical XML. entries/ holds symptoms, diagnoses, and interventions; guides/ holds explanatory documents and navigation. schema/asm-v1.xsd defines the grammar. tools/ implements a reference reader and builder, and examples/query_manual.py is an independent standard-library consumer.

dist/ is disposable output: an HTML site, Markdown reading copies under dist/markdown/, and a JSON catalog. No generated reading copy is checked in. Edit XML, then rebuild. README is the repository landing page, not a duplicate manual entry.

section.title: Identity
section.p: A document has a corpus-wide ID, such as S001. Within a list, members have short local IDs such as multi-read, changed-source, or stalled-edit. The ID is unique only among members of that list; it can be reused in another list or another document.

Singleton sections use their tag names. what-to-record is one prose block with paragraphs, not a list of records. It has no ID. The same principle applies to sections throughout symptoms, diagnoses, and interventions.

References supply scope: S001#observations/multi-read, S001#benign-lookalikes/changed-source, and S001#what-to-record. Those qualified addresses are derived; the source only stores the short local ID on list members.

section.title: Relationships
section.p: A diagnosis references symptom documents. A criterion may reference a symptom too. An intervention reference records its target and the condition under which it applies. Its target already identifies the relationship within the diagnosis. The same protocol can apply to different diagnoses under different conditions.

Singleton sections and repeated objects are both addressable. References to individual observations, lookalikes, examples, criteria, alternatives, preconditions, and steps do not require a filename or a generated heading.

section.title: Interventions
section.p: Interventions remain independent protocols with purpose, preconditions, ordered steps, evaluation, risks, rollback, and uncertainty. An intervention's prose explains its use for investigation and for remediation; a successful outcome does not by itself establish the cause. Structure makes the protocol inspectable; it does not make its applicability automatically decidable or establish that it works.

section.title: Consumers
section.p: The XML format contract and XSD define the draft interface. Any language's XML parser can read it. Consumers can use XML directly or the generated JSON tree and address index. The example consumer imports no ASM implementation code.
A consumer must distinguish format conformance, evidence supporting a category, and confidence in an individual case. They are different claims.

section.title: Current scope
section.p: There remains exactly one symptom, one candidate diagnosis, and one proposed intervention. Entries remain drafts and unvalidated. Severity is deferred. Public hosting, licensing, formal case schemas, and executable assessments are also deferred. The repository remains private.
